newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM urges tough tack on Khmer Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM urges tough tack on Khmer Rouge.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen told a peace rally on Saturday he was prepared to force remaining Khmer Rouge hardliners to join the government.

"I am ready to go to military region number four (in Cambodia's northwest) to order a forced merger in Anlong Veng," the second prime minister told more than 7,000 young students, military, police and Khmer Rouge dissidents who gathered at a Phnom Penh stadium to celebrate moves toward peace in Cambodia.
"Our brothers and sisters there need my presence to help them from the bloody hands of Pol Pot and from opportunity takers who want to delay the forces merging in this area," he said.
Anlong Veng is the stronghold of Khmer Rouge guerrillas loyal to hardline leader Pol Pot, who led the genocidal 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime in Cambodia.

The rebels have been decimated by massive defections in recent months, and only about 800 to 2,000 fighters are believed to remain in the base, which is located near the Thai border in northern Cambodia.
Hun Sen's tough rhetoric was notably at odds with that of his co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh. On Friday, Ranariddh said he would pursue peaceful talks with the remaining guerrillas.
Analysts say tensions between the co-premiers on how to handle Khmer Rouge defectors are worsening, with both leaders continuing to recruit fighters to their own sides.

On a tour of Phnom Malai, a base of dissident guerrillas who broke with hardliners in August and joined with government troops last week, Ranariddh said the rebels deserved at least one general staff position, a move Hun Sen has consistently opposed.
One analyst said Ranariddh continues to raise the issue in an attempt to win over the breakaway group to his party.
